questions.stem: Fiber type Aα is a type of afferent nerve fiber and serves as the sensory fiber of muscle spindle found in muscles. These specific features were described by a physiologist. Select the irrelevant descriptions given:

options.label: A
options.text: Diameter of fiber 12-20 (µm)

options.label: B
options.text: Conduction velocity 70-120 m/s

options.label: C
options.text: Nociceptors

options.label: D
options.text: Primary receptors of muscle spindle

questions.solutionHtml:
Nociceptors

Nociceptors have two different types of axons. The first is the Aδ fiber axons. They are myelinated and can allow an action potential to travel at a rate of about 20 meters/second toward the CNS. The other type is the more slowly conducting C fiber axons.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 229.

questions.stem: Physiologists divided the nerve fibers into specific groups based on the ‘General Classification’ of nerve fibers. Select the incorrect characteristic of nerve fibers in different groups:

options.label: A
options.text: Type C fibers are small unmyelinated nerve fibers that conduct impulses at low velocities.

options.label: B
options.text: Type A fibers are the typically large and medium-sized myelinated fibers of spinal nerves.

options.label: C
options.text: Type A fibers are further subdivided into α, β, and δ fibers.

options.label: D
options.text: Subset of type A fibers has conduction velocity between 70-120 m/s.

questions.answerText: Type A fibers are further subdivided into α, β, and δ fibers.
questions.solutionHtml:
Type A fibers are further subdivided into α, β, and δ fibers.

Subsets of type A fibers are α, β, γ, and δ fibers.



Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 591

questions.stem: A patient at the age of 36 years presented with severe toothache and swelling in the right left side of the face about the upper 1st molar tooth for the past 4 days. The dentist advised immediate abscess drainage under local anesthetic infiltration. The dentist injected 2% lignocaine in the mucosa and operated on the tooth. Select the irrelevant statements:

options.label: A
options.text: Type A fibers are most sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics.

options.label: B
options.text: Type A fibers are the least sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics.

options.label: C
options.text: Type C fibers are most sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics.

options.label: D
options.text: Type B fibers have intermediate sensitivity to the effect of local anesthetics.

questions.answerText: Type A fibers are most sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics.
questions.solutionHtml:
Type A fibers are most sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics.

Type A fibers are not the most sensitive to the effect of local anesthetics but exhibit the least sensitivity.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 230-231.

questions.stem: Pain is “an unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage or described in terms of such damage. Select the irrelevant description about pain:

options.label: A
options.text: Injured tissues release Na+ ions that depolarize nerve terminals.

options.label: B
options.text: Injured tissues release bradykinin and substance P.

options.label: C
options.text: Histamine is released from mast cells.

options.label: D
options.text: Serotonin (5-HT) is released by platelets.

questions.answerText: Injured tissues release Na+ ions that depolarize nerve terminals.
questions.solutionHtml:
Injured tissues release Na+ ions that depolarize nerve terminals.

Injured tissues do not release Na+ ions but K+ ions that depolarize nerve terminals.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 394.

questions.stem: Neurologist while explaining the pain physiology, mentioned that damaged nerve fibers undergo sprouting. This can explain why innocuous stimuli can induce pain after an injury. Select the incorrect statement:

options.label: A
options.text: Synergistic effect of substance P and glutamate from nociceptive afferents in the spinal cord.

options.label: B
options.text: Excessive activation of GABA receptors on spinal neurons.

options.label: C
options.text: “wind-up” phenomenon

options.label: D
options.text: Raised activity in pain-transmitting pathways

questions.answerText: Excessive activation of GABA receptors on spinal neurons.
questions.solutionHtml:
Excessive activation of GABA receptors on spinal neurons.

Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is an amino acid that functions as the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter for the central nervous system (CNS). It functions to reduce neuronal excitability by inhibiting nerve transmission.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 394.

questions.stem: A male patient aged 67 years presented with nauseating pain and a burning sensation when passing urine with frequent urination at night past 3 days. Physicians described the physiology of such types of pain to scholars. Select the irrelevant explanation for the type of pain experienced by the patient:

options.label: A
options.text: Presence of Aδ nerve fibers in deep tissues.

options.label: B
options.text: Nociceptors are present in visceral organs.

options.label: C
options.text: Afferent fibers from visceral structures enter CNS via sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves.

options.label: D
options.text: Deep pain and visceral pain are poorly localized, nauseating, and with sweating.

questions.answerText: Presence of Aδ nerve fibers in deep tissues.
questions.solutionHtml:
Presence of Aδ nerve fibers in deep tissues.

There is a relative deficiency of Aδ nerve fibers in deep structures, so there is little rapid, sharp pain.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 395-396.

questions.stem: A patient aged 23 years, was taken to the hospital with chest pain radiating to the left shoulder, and arm, tightness over the chest, and sweating. Persons who escorted the patient gave H/O of starting pain when the patient was working in the office. The patient kept the tablet below the tongue but it had no effect. Select the irrelevant statement:

options.label: A
options.text: Divergence of somatic and visceral pain. Fibers from the second-order neurons in the dorsal horn

options.label: B
options.text: Referred pain

options.label: C
options.text: Tissue of pain origin and tissue of pain felt have the same development from the same dermatome

options.label: D
options.text: Convergence projection theory

questions.answerText: Divergence of somatic and visceral pain. Fibers from the second-order neurons in the dorsal horn
questions.solutionHtml:
Divergence of somatic and visceral pain. Fibers from the second-order neurons in the dorsal horn

Visceral pain often radiates or is referred to other areas. Irritation of a visceral organ frequently produces pain that is felt not at that site but in a somatic structure that may be some distance away (referred pain).



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 395-396-397.
